knowledge_point.title: Solving a System of Equations by Eliminating the First Variable

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-5y &=9 \\ 5x+6y &=14\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The solution $(x,y)$ to this system is $($
{{field-1}}$\,,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the coefficient of $x$ in the  first  equation is $1,$ while in the second equation it is $5.$ 

If we multiply the first equation by $-5,$ then the $x$-coefficient will become $-5,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $5$ in the second equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}(\,x-5y &=9\,)\,\times (-5) \\ 5x+6y &=14\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,\left\{\begin{aligned}-5x+25y &=-45 \\ 5x+6y &=14\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $x$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\cancel{5x}+25y & =-45 \\ \cancel{5x}+6y & =14 \\ (25y+6y) & =(-45+14) \\ 31y & =-31 \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $y=-1.$ However, we still need to find $x.$ To do this, we substitute $y=-1$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5y & =9 \\ x-5(-1) & =9 \\ x+5 & =9 \\ x & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=4,\,y=-1,$ which can be expressed as $(4,-1).$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}9x+y &=-6 \\ -3x+5y &=18\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The solution $(x,y)$ to this system is $($
{{field-1}}$\,,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the coefficient of $x$ in the  first  equation is $9,$ while in the second equation it is $-3.$ 

If we multiply the second equation by $3,$ then the $x$-coefficient will become $-9,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $9$ in the first equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}9x+y &=-6 \\ (\,-3x+5y &=18\,)\,\times (3)\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,\left\{\begin{aligned}9x+y &=-6 \\ -9x+15y &=54\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $x$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{9x}+y & =-6 \\ -\cancel{9x}+15y & =54 \\ (y+15y) & =(-6+54) \\ 16y & =48 \\ y & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $y=3.$ However, we still need to find $x.$ To do this, we substitute $y=3$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}9x+y & =-6 \\ 9x+(3) & =-6 \\ 9x+3 & =-6 \\ 9x & =-9 \\ x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-1,\,y=3,$ which can be expressed as $(-1,3).$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3s+7t &=-38 \\ 15s+2t &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The solution $(s,t)$ to this system is $($
{{field-1}}$\,,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the coefficient of $s$ in the  first  equation is $-3,$ while in the second equation it is $15.$ 

If we multiply the first equation by $5,$ then the $s$-coefficient will become $-15,$ which will cancel with the coefficient of $15$ in the second equation.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}(\,-3s+7t &=-38\,)\,\times (5) \\ 15s+2t &=5\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,\left\{\begin{aligned}-15s+35t &=-190 \\ 15s+2t &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable $s$ will be eliminated:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\cancel{15s}+35t & =-190 \\ \cancel{15s}+2t & =5 \\ (35t+2t) & =(-190+5) \\ 37t & =-185 \\ t & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $t=-5.$ However, we still need to find $s.$ To do this, we substitute $t=-5$ back into one of the equations. Let's choose the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3s+7t & =-38 \\ -3s+7(-5) & =-38 \\ -3s-35 & =-38 \\ -3s & =-3 \\ s & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $s=1,\,t=-5,$ which can be expressed as $(1,-5).$
